question.leadin: Answer the following about World War I.
question.text: Led by Franz Joseph the First, this dual-monarchy declared war on Serbia in July 1914.
question.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary (accept Austro-Hungarian Empire/Monarchy; do not prompt on partial answer)
question.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

swap.leadin: A bomb thrown at this leader's convertible bounced off and detonated under a nearby car.
swap.text: Name this Austrian archduke and heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, whose assassination was one of the pivotal causes of World War I.
swap.answerHtml: Archduke Franz Ferdinand (or Franz Ferdinand Carl Ludwig Joseph Maria of Austria)
swap.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

question.leadin: The fates of the remnants of both the Holy Roman Empire and post-Napoleonic France were debated in this city.
question.text: Name this Austrian city, site of an 1814-1815 Congress.
question.clue: Originally, Joachim Murat was allowed to remain king of Naples by the terms established here, and participants at this eventincluded Prince von Hardenburg, Viscount Castlereagh, and Count Nesselrode.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about scandals in the French Third Republic.
swap.text: This Austrian reporter's experiences of anti-Semitism in the Dreyfus affair and elsewhere led him to plan the First Zionist Conference.
swap.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

question.leadin: This country formed a union with one of its neighbors in the Compromise of 1867.
question.text: Name this country that formed a dual monarchy with Hungary as a result of the Ausgleich.
question.clue: This state deliberately provoked an 1846 serf rebellion in order to counter revolutionary szlachta.

swap.leadin: In the 18th century, Austria was not exactly friendly to the idea of a female ruler.
swap.text: Name this Austrian ruler whose father Charles VI attempted to facilitate her ascension to the throne with the passage of the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713.
swap.clue: To govern compulsory peasant labor, this monarch issued the Robot Patent.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Congress of Vienna.
question.text: This Austrian statesman, who resigned after the revolutions of 1848, orchestrated the Congress of Vienna. This man succeeded Johann Stadion as Foreign Minister after the Battle of Wagram.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.text: Dollfuss' successor, Kurt Schuschnigg, was powerless to stop Hitler's annexation of Austria, an event usually given this name from the German for "connection."
swap.clue: Kurt von Schuschnigg was replaced by Arthur Seyss-Inquart the day before this event, which gathered 99.7% approval in a plebiscite a month after it happened.

question.text: The over-the-top Soviet war memorial in Schwarzenbergplatz in this country's capital city has been targeted by vandals, but it is protected by the 1955 treaty by which Soviet troops ended their occupation of part this country.
question.clue: A United Nations Secretary General from this country received a telegram from Idi Amin that praised the Munich Massacre during his service from 1972 to 1981.

swap.leadin: This city's fin-de-siecle(fan duh SYECK-luh) culture involved many discussions in coffeehouses, and is the subject of a book by Karl Schorske.
swap.text: Name this city once governed by Karl Lueger, who declared "it is up to me to decide who is a Jew."
swap.clue: Terrible weather and Nikola Jurisic's stand at Guns played a part in the second failed siege of this city by Suleiman the Magnificent.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the city of Pressburg.
question.text: The War of the Third Coalition was ended by the 1805 Peace of Pressburg between Napoleon and this final Holy Roman Emperor. Along with Tsar Alexander I of Russia, this emperor was defeated at the Battle of Austerlitz.
question.clue: Name that French monarch who had earlier challenged Charles in the election for Holy Roman Emperor.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about lesser-known "Wars of Succession" from European history.
swap.text: The War of Bavarian Succession saw this Habsburg co-regent of his mother, Maria Theresa, lead his men in the field in Bavaria against Frederick the Great's men, with the Peace of Teschen seeing a small territorial gain for Austria.
swap.clue: His first wife Isabella of Parma died of smallpox long before that blunder in the Battle of Karansebes.

question.leadin: You are an assassin. Answer some questions about your deeds.
question.text: It's 1914. You are a Bosnian Serb and member of the Black Hand Gavrilo Princip, who will assassinate this Archduke and his wife Sophie, setting off a chain of events that will begin World War I.
question.clue: This nephew of Franz Josef became heir presumptive after the suicide of Crown Prince Rudolf and his own father's death. His assassination by Bosnian nationalist Gavrilo Princip set off the July Crisis.

swap.text: Before Balfour, Joseph Chamberlain worked with this man to establish a temporary Jewish homeland in the Uganda Scheme. This founder of Zionism discussed the "Jewish Question" in his 1895 pamphlet Der Judenstaat ("dare YOO-den-shtaht").
swap.clue: With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man.

question.text: This man served as secretary general from 1972 to 1981. He was elected president of Austria in 1986 despite revelations that he served as an interpreter and intelligence officer to a German unit in World War II that committed war crimes.
question.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

swap.text: Your belief in Central Power unity was probably shattered following this affair late in the war. In this affair, Clemenceau published Emperor Charles I's correspondence with the namesake person asking for peace with the Allies.

question.leadin: He founded the Fatherland Front as a conservative coalition to support his rule, outlawing all other parties.
question.text: Name this chancellor of Austria who served as its dictator beginning in 1933 until he was assassinated by the Nazis a year later as part of the July Putsch.
question.clue: This dictator absorbed the Heimwehr of Prince Starhemberg to establish the Fatherland Front, but was assassinated by Otto Planetta during the July Putsch.

swap.leadin: Historians have identified many similarities between investiture ceremonies in Ireland and those in this duchy, during which a peasant sitting on a stone would ask questions "in the Slavic tongue"
swap.text: Name this duchy ruled by Bernhard von Spanheim. After the death of its duke Henry VI in 1335, the Habsburgs were enfeoffed ("en-fiefed") by Emperor Ludwig IV with this duchy and a neighbouring march.
swap.answerHtml: Duchy of Carinthia [or Herzogtum Kärnten or Vojvodina Koroška; accept Carinthia and Carniola; accept Carantania; do NOT accept Carniola alone, which wasn’t a duchy itself at a time and none of the clues directly apply to it]

question.leadin: This man's election was vetoed three times by Franz Joseph, who despised him.
question.text: Name this mayor of Vienna from 1897 - 1910, whose virulent anti-semitism may have inspired a young Adolf Hitler.

swap.text: Frederick was less enthused about this treaty, through which Louis XIV forced him to give up his Pomeranian holdings won at Fehrbellin in the Scanian War. Karl Renner was also forced by the French to sign a treaty by this name in the wake of the Battle of Vittorio Veneto.
swap.answerHtml: Treaty of Saint Germain-en-Laye [do not accept or prompt on “Saint-Germain”]
